description:
v0.3.0 shipped a broken wheel to PyPI because an optional dependency loaded on
a CLI startup path that nothing tested. The contract test the team believed
guarded this (tests/unit/test_package_dependencies.py) does NOT exist on
develop (no git history at that path); the surviving startup test
(tests/unit/cli/test_cli_startup_imports.py) only asserts that runner/monitoring
and textcharts setup-help modules are absent - it makes NO assertion about heavy
optional deps.

A live import trace on develop @ cb49cecf5 shows the leak is real and
entry-point-specific:
  - `import benchbox` eagerly loads duckdb, psycopg, boto3, google, cloudpathlib
    (NOT pandas/polars/pyarrow - drop-pandas-from-core worked).
  - `benchbox --help` additionally loads pandas, polars, pyarrow.
Verified culprits (first benchbox frame that triggers each):
  - duckdb / psycopg     <- benchbox/platforms/__init__.py:252 (eager
                            _load_optional_adapter of concrete adapters)
  - boto3/google/cloudpathlib <- benchbox/core/benchmark_result_validation.py:8
                            -> benchbox/utils/cloud_storage.py:22 (top-level
                            cloudpathlib import)
  - pandas               <- benchbox/utils/format_converters/__init__.py:16
                            -> parquet_converter.py:15
  - pyarrow              <- benchbox/utils/format_converters/__init__.py:7
                            -> format_converters/base.py:15
  - polars               <- benchbox/platforms/dataframe/__init__.py:60
                            -> polars_df.py:36
  - the CLI command surface <- benchbox/cli/main.py:8 re-exports every command;
                            benchbox/cli/commands/__init__.py:9 eagerly imports
                            all command modules; BenchBoxGroup.format_commands
                            (benchbox/cli/help.py:383) calls get_command() per
                            subcommand, re-importing bodies during top-level help.

The common root cause is the same throughout: package __init__ modules (and the
cli.main compat shim) eagerly import concrete heavy submodules. One consistent
technique - defer to lazy resolution - fixes every hub. This item pins the
contract with a test FIRST, then makes each hub lazy, then wires the test (and a
two-mode pre-publish wheel smoke) into CI so the regression cannot recur.

anti_patterns.dont: fix the leak by removing functionality or dropping a dependency from a path that needs it at call time
anti_patterns.why: defer the import, do not delete the feature.

anti_patterns.dont: rely on an in-process CliRunner for the --help isolation assertion
anti_patterns.why: it shares the test session's sys.modules and will give a false PASS; invoke a fresh interpreter/subprocess.

deferrals.reason:
After the in-scope lazy refactor, tests/unit/test_import_isolation.py is down to
boto3/google/cloudpathlib failures only. The verified remaining path is
benchbox/__init__.py eagerly importing FlightData, which imports
benchbox/utils/datagen_manifest.py, whose top-level cloudpathlib import loads
cloudpathlib plus boto3/google provider SDKs. Both benchbox/__init__.py and
benchbox/utils/datagen_manifest.py are outside this TODO's scope_limit.only_modify,
so the contract cannot be made green without widening scope.

deferrals.summary: Make the remaining cloud-path import path lazy outside this TODO's file allowlist.

preserves.behavior: Bare installs without an optional extra still degrade gracefully (clear 'platform unavailable' message), never crash, for both ImportError and OSError.
Every CLI command and its help text remain available and unchanged; benchbox <cmd> --help and command execution paths keep working.
No behavior change to command logic; this is an import-time/laziness refactor only.

work_units.notes:
New tests/unit/test_import_isolation.py, subprocess-based (one clean
interpreter per case so the test session's own imports do not pollute
sys.modules), parametrized per dep so failures are individually legible.
Assert NONE of {pandas, polars, pyarrow, duckdb, psycopg, boto3, google,
cloudpathlib} appear in sys.modules after each of: `import benchbox`,
`import benchbox.cli.main`, and `benchbox --help` (via subprocess invocation
of the console entry, not an in-process CliRunner that shares sys.modules).
Mark it fast. It supersedes the narrow assertions in
tests/unit/cli/test_cli_startup_imports.py (keep that file's runner/monitoring
checks; do not duplicate). This pins the contract before any refactor.

work_units.notes:
A lazy Click group alone does NOT fix `import benchbox.cli.main`; all three
parts are required or the CLI path stays heavy:
  (i)  Entrypoint: move the console script from benchbox.cli.main:main
       (pyproject.toml:370) to benchbox.cli.app:main, and reduce
       benchbox/cli/main.py to a compat shim that re-exports cli/main/command
       symbols lazily via module-level __getattr__ (PEP 562) so importing it
       no longer eagerly binds command objects.
  (ii) Command fan-out: benchbox/cli/commands/__init__.py:9 imports every
       command module. Convert to lazy per-command resolution (string
       "module:callback" registry resolved on first use).
  (iii) Static help: BenchBoxGroup.format_commands (benchbox/cli/help.py:383)
       calls self.get_command() per subcommand, re-importing bodies during
       top-level help. Render from static command metadata (name + short help
       held in the registry) so `benchbox --help` never imports command
       bodies.
Acceptance is BOTH that w0's benchbox.cli.main + --help cases pass AND that
the full command list and help text are unchanged (snapshot/list test), and
`benchbox <cmd> --help` plus execution paths still work.
work_units.summary: Make benchbox.cli.main itself lean - entrypoint, command fan-out, and static help (three parts)
